---
title: "Run a sandbox model with deSolve (R)"
format: html
---

**Illustrative simulation: not a forecast, not fitted to data.**

The sandbox's "Copy as code" button produces R code like the block below for any model. This example is the SEIR
teaching model with a contact reduction between day 20 and day 60, followed by a one-way sweep. It uses no reported data.

```{r}
library(deSolve)
BASE <- list(beta = 0.5, gamma = 0.2, sigma = 1 / 3)
INTERVENTIONS <- list(list(kind = "scale", name = "beta", value = 0.5, start = 20, end = 60))
params_at <- function(t, base = BASE) {
  p <- base
  for (iv in INTERVENTIONS) if (t >= iv$start && t < iv$end) p[[iv$name]] <- if (iv$kind == "scale") p[[iv$name]] * iv$value else iv$value
  p
}
rhs <- function(t, y, parms) {
  p <- params_at(t, parms); N <- sum(y)
  inf <- p$beta * y[1] * y[3] / N; prog <- p$sigma * y[2]; rec <- p$gamma * y[3]
  list(c(-inf, inf - prog, prog - rec, rec))
}
Y0 <- c(S = 9995, E = 0, I = 5, R = 0)
times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 160, by = 1), 20, 60)))
out <- as.data.frame(ode(y = Y0, times = times, func = rhs, parms = BASE, method = "lsoda", rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-10))
stopifnot(all(abs(rowSums(out[, -1]) - 10000) < 1e-5))   # population is conserved
out[which.max(out$I), ]
```

```{r}
# One-way sweep: the simulated peak for a range of transmission rates. This explores the model; it estimates nothing.
sapply(seq(0.25, 0.75, by = 0.1), function(b) {
  o <- as.data.frame(ode(y = Y0, times = times, func = rhs, parms = modifyList(BASE, list(beta = b)), method = "lsoda"))
  max(o$I)
})
```
